added_models.model: Isogenic RPGR-knockout human iPSC retinal organoids, AAV-RPGR clinical construct (bota-vec)

engagement.model: Isogenic RPGR-knockout human iPSC retinal organoids, AAV-RPGR clinical construct (bota-vec)
engagement.note: AAV-RPGR restored RPGR protein, glutamylation and connecting-cilium localisation and corrected rhodopsin mislocalisation in KO organoids; none is measured in patients.
engagement.short: Organoid RPGR and opsin readouts restored
engagement.quote: The transduction of RPGR-KO ROs using AAV-RPGR successfully restored RPGR mRNA and protein expression and localisation to the photoreceptor connecting cilium in rod and cone photoreceptors.
engagement.judgement: RPGR localisation and opsin trafficking cannot be sampled in dosed patients' retinas, so engagement stays untested.

efficacy.model: Isogenic RPGR-knockout human iPSC retinal organoids, AAV-RPGR clinical construct (bota-vec)
efficacy.note: Clinical bota-vec construct rescued opsin localisation in human RPGR-KO organoids, framed as supporting phase 1/2 and the ongoing phase 3.
efficacy.short: Organoids support bota-vec ahead of LUMEOS
efficacy.quote: These data provide mechanistic insights into RPGR ORF15 gene supplementation functional potency in human photoreceptor cells and support the previously reported Phase I/II trial positive results using this vector construct in patients with RPGR-associated XLRP
efficacy.judgement: The phase 1/2 trial's primary outcome was safety, so the organoids' agreement with its secondary efficacy signals is not scored as retro; LUMEOS is the first primary-endpoint test.

efficacy.model: Isogenic RPGR-knockout human iPSC retinal organoids, AAV-RPGR clinical construct (bota-vec)
efficacy.note: LUMEOS phase 3 (n=95) missed its vision-guided mobility primary endpoint after the organoids had supported bota-vec.
efficacy.quote: The novel primary endpoint to assess the effect of bilaterial treatment with bota-vec on functional vision as measured by a Visual Mobility Assessment (VMA), or maze, did not meet statistical significance.
efficacy.confidence_note: Sponsor SEC exhibit (16 Apr 2026); J&J first released the miss on 2 May 2025 (Fierce Biotech, 5 May 2025); the J&J Medical Connect page now returns 404. No peer-reviewed or registry results yet.
efficacy.judgement: Paired comparison: organoid paper predates the phase 3 readout, so it is prospective; secondary-endpoint gains do not change a primary-endpoint miss.

patient_trials.quote: Change From Baseline to Week 52 in Vision-guided Mobility Assessment (VMA) as Measured by the Ability of the Participant to Navigate Through a VMA Maze
